cases.prompt: What is the company's policy on remote work eligibility?
cases.context: Employee Handbook 4.2: Employees who have completed their six-month probation are eligible to work remotely up to three days per week, subject to manager approval. Roles requiring on-site lab access are excluded.
rubric: Faithfulness: every claim is supported by the context
Completeness: states the three-days-per-week limit and probation requirement
Groundedness: notes manager approval and the lab-access exclusion
cases.referenceAnswer: Employees past their six-month probation may work remotely up to three days per week with manager approval; roles needing on-site lab access are excluded.

cases.prompt: How many vacation days do new employees receive in their first year?
cases.context: Benefits Guide: New full-time employees accrue 1.25 vacation days per month worked in their first calendar year, up to a maximum of 15 days. Unused days may carry over up to 5 days into the next year.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses only the accrual figures from the context
Completeness: mentions the 15-day first-year maximum
Groundedness: mentions the 5-day carryover rule
cases.referenceAnswer: New full-time employees accrue 1.25 days per month, up to 15 days in the first year, with up to 5 unused days carried over.

cases.prompt: What is the data retention period for customer support tickets?
cases.context: Data Governance 7.1: Customer support tickets and attachments are retained for 24 months from closure, after which they are permanently deleted unless subject to a legal hold.
rubric: Faithfulness: states 24 months without inventing other periods
Completeness: ties retention to the date of closure
Groundedness: mentions the legal-hold exception
cases.referenceAnswer: Support tickets are retained for 24 months from closure, then permanently deleted unless under a legal hold.

cases.prompt: What expense approval is required for purchases over 1000 dollars?
cases.context: Finance Policy 3.4: Purchases up to 1000 dollars may be approved by a team lead. Purchases above 1000 dollars require director approval, and above 10000 dollars require VP approval.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses only the stated approval tiers
Completeness: states director approval for over 1000 dollars
Groundedness: mentions the VP tier above 10000 dollars
cases.referenceAnswer: Purchases above 1000 dollars require director approval, and those above 10000 dollars require VP approval.

cases.prompt: What is the SLA response time for a critical (P1) incident?
cases.context: Service Level Agreement: P1 (critical) incidents receive a response within 15 minutes and a resolution target of 4 hours. P2 incidents have a 1-hour response. Coverage is 24x7.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the P1 figures from the context
Completeness: states the 15-minute response
Groundedness: mentions the 4-hour resolution target
cases.referenceAnswer: P1 critical incidents get a response within 15 minutes and target resolution within 4 hours, under 24x7 coverage.

cases.prompt: Which password requirements apply to employee accounts?
cases.context: Security Policy 2.1: Passwords must be at least 12 characters, include upper and lower case letters, a number and a symbol, and be rotated every 90 days. Reuse of the last 5 passwords is prohibited.
rubric: Faithfulness: states only the listed requirements
Completeness: mentions the 12-character minimum and 90-day rotation
Groundedness: mentions the no-reuse-of-last-5 rule
cases.referenceAnswer: Passwords need at least 12 characters with mixed case, a number and a symbol, must rotate every 90 days, and cannot reuse the last 5 passwords.

cases.prompt: How long is the warranty on company-issued laptops?
cases.context: IT Asset Policy: Company laptops carry a 3-year manufacturer warranty. Batteries are covered for 1 year. Accidental damage is not covered and is charged to the department.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated warranty periods
Completeness: states the 3-year laptop warranty
Groundedness: notes the 1-year battery coverage and accidental-damage exclusion
cases.referenceAnswer: Laptops have a 3-year manufacturer warranty; batteries are covered for 1 year, and accidental damage is excluded and charged to the department.

cases.prompt: What is the notice period for resignation?
cases.context: HR Policy 9.0: Employees must give at least four weeks' written notice of resignation. Managers and above must give eight weeks. Unused notice may be offset against accrued leave with approval.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated notice periods
Completeness: states four weeks for employees and eight for managers
Groundedness: mentions offsetting against accrued leave with approval
cases.referenceAnswer: Employees must give at least four weeks' written notice and managers eight weeks; unused notice can be offset against accrued leave with approval.

cases.prompt: What are the office hours for the Taipei site?
cases.context: Facilities Notice: The Taipei office is open 08:30 to 18:00 on weekdays. Badge access is required outside these hours. The office is closed on national holidays.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated hours
Completeness: states 08:30 to 18:00 on weekdays
Groundedness: mentions badge access after hours and holiday closure
cases.referenceAnswer: The Taipei office is open 08:30 to 18:00 on weekdays, needs badge access outside those hours, and is closed on national holidays.

cases.prompt: What is the reimbursement rate for personal vehicle mileage?
cases.context: Travel Policy 5.2: Personal vehicle use is reimbursed at 0.30 dollars per kilometer. Tolls and parking are reimbursed with receipts. Daily commuting to the regular office is not reimbursable.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated rate
Completeness: states 0.30 dollars per kilometer
Groundedness: notes tolls/parking with receipts and the commuting exclusion
cases.referenceAnswer: Personal vehicle mileage is reimbursed at 0.30 dollars per kilometer, with tolls and parking on receipts; regular commuting is not reimbursable.

cases.prompt: Who is authorized to approve a production database change?
cases.context: Change Management 6.3: Production database changes require approval from the database owner and a peer reviewer, and must be scheduled in a change window. Emergency changes need post-hoc review within 24 hours.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated approvers
Completeness: states the database owner and peer reviewer
Groundedness: mentions the change window and emergency post-hoc review
cases.referenceAnswer: Production database changes need the database owner and a peer reviewer to approve and must run in a change window; emergency changes get post-hoc review within 24 hours.

cases.prompt: What is the maximum file size for email attachments?
cases.context: IT Guidelines: Email attachments are limited to 25 MB. Larger files should be shared via the document portal with a link. Executable attachments are blocked by the mail gateway.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated limit
Completeness: states the 25 MB limit
Groundedness: mentions the portal for larger files and blocked executables
cases.referenceAnswer: Email attachments are capped at 25 MB; larger files go through the document portal link, and executable attachments are blocked.

cases.prompt: What training is required before accessing customer data?
cases.context: Compliance 1.4: All staff must complete annual data-privacy training and sign the confidentiality agreement before accessing customer data. Access is revoked if training lapses.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated requirements
Completeness: mentions annual data-privacy training
Groundedness: notes the confidentiality agreement and revocation on lapse
cases.referenceAnswer: Before accessing customer data, staff must complete annual data-privacy training and sign the confidentiality agreement; access is revoked if training lapses.

cases.prompt: How is on-call compensation handled?
cases.context: Compensation Addendum: On-call engineers receive a flat 50 dollars per on-call day plus 1.5x hourly pay for time spent actively responding to incidents. On-call rotates weekly.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated figures
Completeness: states the 50-dollar daily stipend
Groundedness: mentions 1.5x active-response pay and weekly rotation
cases.referenceAnswer: On-call engineers get a flat 50 dollars per on-call day plus 1.5x hourly pay for active incident response, with weekly rotation.

cases.prompt: What is the policy on using open-source software in products?
cases.context: Open Source Policy 2.2: Permissively licensed components (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) are pre-approved. Copyleft licenses (GPL) require legal review. All usage must be recorded in the software bill of materials.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated license categories
Completeness: notes permissive licenses are pre-approved
Groundedness: mentions GPL legal review and the SBOM recording
cases.referenceAnswer: Permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD) are pre-approved, copyleft (GPL) needs legal review, and all use must be recorded in the software bill of materials.

cases.prompt: What backup schedule applies to production systems?
cases.context: Backup Policy 4.1: Production systems are backed up incrementally every 6 hours and fully every night. Backups are retained for 30 days and replicated to a second region.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated schedule
Completeness: mentions 6-hourly incremental and nightly full backups
Groundedness: notes the 30-day retention and cross-region replication
cases.referenceAnswer: Production is backed up incrementally every 6 hours and fully each night, retained for 30 days and replicated to a second region.

cases.prompt: What is the dress code for client meetings?
cases.context: Office Etiquette: Business-casual attire is expected for client meetings. Company-branded shirts are acceptable. Casual wear is allowed on internal-only days.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated dress code
Completeness: states business-casual for client meetings
Groundedness: notes branded shirts and casual internal days
cases.referenceAnswer: Client meetings expect business-casual attire, with company-branded shirts acceptable; casual wear is fine on internal-only days.

cases.prompt: How long are interview feedback records kept?
cases.context: Recruiting Policy 8.5: Interview feedback and scorecards are kept for 12 months for unsuccessful candidates and for the duration of employment plus 12 months for hires.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated retention periods
Completeness: states 12 months for unsuccessful candidates
Groundedness: notes employment-plus-12-months for hires
cases.referenceAnswer: Interview feedback is kept for 12 months for unsuccessful candidates and for employment plus 12 months for hires.

cases.prompt: What is the company's stance on accepting gifts from vendors?
cases.context: Ethics Policy 3.1: Employees may accept token gifts under 50 dollars. Gifts above this value must be declined or reported to compliance. Cash gifts are never permitted.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated thresholds
Completeness: states the 50-dollar token limit
Groundedness: notes reporting above the limit and the cash prohibition
cases.referenceAnswer: Token gifts under 50 dollars may be accepted; anything above must be declined or reported to compliance, and cash gifts are never allowed.

cases.prompt: What environments must a change pass before production?
cases.context: Release Process 2.0: Changes must pass automated tests in development, then staging with a manual sign-off, before promotion to production. Hotfixes may skip staging with director approval.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated environments
Completeness: states development then staging before production
Groundedness: notes the staging manual sign-off and hotfix exception
cases.referenceAnswer: Changes pass automated tests in development, then staging with manual sign-off, before production; hotfixes may skip staging with director approval.

cases.prompt: What is the parental leave entitlement?
cases.context: Leave Policy 11.2: Eligible employees receive 12 weeks of paid parental leave, which may be taken within 12 months of the birth or adoption. An additional 4 weeks unpaid is available on request.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated entitlements
Completeness: states 12 weeks paid leave
Groundedness: notes the 12-month window and optional 4 unpaid weeks
cases.referenceAnswer: Eligible employees get 12 weeks of paid parental leave within 12 months of birth or adoption, plus an optional 4 unpaid weeks on request.

cases.prompt: What logging is required for access to sensitive systems?
cases.context: Audit Policy 5.0: All access to sensitive systems must be logged with user, timestamp, and action. Logs are immutable and retained for 1 year. Access without a corresponding ticket is flagged.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated logging requirements
Completeness: mentions user, timestamp and action
Groundedness: notes immutable 1-year retention and ticket flagging
cases.referenceAnswer: Access to sensitive systems must be logged with user, timestamp and action; logs are immutable, retained 1 year, and access without a ticket is flagged.

cases.prompt: What is the refund window for enterprise subscriptions?
cases.context: Sales Terms 4.4: Enterprise subscriptions may be refunded in full within 30 days of purchase. After 30 days, refunds are prorated for the unused term. Setup fees are non-refundable.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated windows
Completeness: states the 30-day full-refund window
Groundedness: notes prorated refunds after 30 days and non-refundable setup fees
cases.referenceAnswer: Enterprise subscriptions are fully refundable within 30 days; after that refunds are prorated for the unused term, and setup fees are non-refundable.

cases.prompt: What approval is needed to publish a public blog post?
cases.context: Communications Policy 7.2: Public blog posts require review by the marketing lead and, for technical content, a subject-matter expert. Posts mentioning customers need customer consent on file.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated approvals
Completeness: mentions the marketing lead review
Groundedness: notes the SME review and customer-consent requirement
cases.referenceAnswer: Public blog posts need marketing-lead review plus a subject-matter expert for technical content, and customer consent on file if customers are mentioned.

cases.prompt: What is the escalation path for an unresolved P2 incident?
cases.context: Incident Policy 6.6: A P2 incident unresolved after 2 hours is escalated to the on-call manager; after 4 hours, to the engineering director. A status update is posted hourly.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated escalation path
Completeness: states escalation to the on-call manager after 2 hours
Groundedness: notes director escalation after 4 hours and hourly updates
cases.referenceAnswer: An unresolved P2 escalates to the on-call manager after 2 hours and the engineering director after 4 hours, with hourly status updates.

cases.prompt: How are software license seats reclaimed?
cases.context: License Management 3.3: Seats unused for 60 consecutive days are automatically reclaimed and returned to the pool. Users are notified 7 days before reclamation and can request to keep the seat.
rubric: Faithfulness: uses the stated rules
Completeness: states reclamation after 60 unused days
Groundedness: notes the 7-day notice and keep-request option
cases.referenceAnswer: Seats unused for 60 consecutive days are auto-reclaimed to the pool, with a 7-day notice during which the user can request to keep the seat.

cases.prompt: What is the policy on storing data outside the home region?

Groundedness: notes the documented need, DPO approval, and that backups follow the same rule
cases.referenceAnswer: Customer data must stay in its designated region; cross-region transfer needs a documented business need and data-protection-officer approval, and backups follow the same rule.

cases.prompt: What is the meeting-room booking cancellation policy?
cases.context: Facilities Booking: Meeting rooms not checked in within 15 minutes of the start time are automatically released. Recurring bookings unused for two consecutive weeks are cancelled.

Completeness: states the 15-minute auto-release
Groundedness: notes cancellation of recurring bookings unused for two weeks
cases.referenceAnswer: Rooms not checked in within 15 minutes are auto-released, and recurring bookings unused for two consecutive weeks are cancelled.

cases.prompt: What are the requirements for a valid expense receipt?

Groundedness: notes the handwritten-receipt rule and the over-75 rejection
cases.referenceAnswer: Valid receipts must show vendor, date, itemized amount and currency; handwritten ones need a manager note, and expenses over 75 dollars without a receipt are rejected.
